4. In respect of paragraph a., it was mentioned at paragraph 24 of my 1st Witness Statement that a total of 74 bodies and/or body parts were found in the search operation conducted by the DVIU’s Recovery Teams. Such 74 bodies and/or body parts did not include S/N 166, as the body part of S/N 166 was in fact recovered by the forensic pathologist (who was not part of the DVIU) in the absence of the DVIU at Room ██████████████████ on 19 December 2025. Hence, S/N 166 was not included in the breakdown of the said 74 bodies and/or body parts mentioned at paragraph 27 and Annex 1 of my 1st Witness Statement. In this regard, I understand that it was stated in the Pol.75 Findings of S/N 166 (which was submitted to the Committee under the 8th Lists of Contents – Part VI-H1-142c) and the Composite List that S/N 166 was discovered on 1 December 2025. 1 December 2025 was the date on which possible remains were found but, upon examination, S/N 166 could not be identified from those possible remains, which were only of S/N 131.

5. In the light of paragraph 4 above, it is confirmed that a total of 10 fatalities (S/N 131, 148, 149, 151, 153, 159, 160, 161, 163 & 165) were identified from 5 bags of body parts (Part VI-E1-39, 50, 55, 59 & 65). S/N 166 was not identified from any one of the said 5 bags. Therefore, it resulted in +5 additional body parts.

6. In response to paragraph b., it is confirmed that a total of 4 samples (Part VI-E1-19, 29, 31 & 63) were duplicated with 3 existing fatalities (S/N 73, 112 & 119).

7. It follows that, in response to paragraph c., the DVIU had handled the bodies and/or body parts belonging to a total number of 62 fatalities (S/N 73, 103-153, 158-165, 167 & 168).
